title: DevSecOps and DevOps: what actually changes in the routine

videos.script: A scanner was bought last year. It runs on every push. {{red}} It has been red for a month, and nobody reads it any more. {{ignored}} That is the most common way DevSecOps fails. Nothing about the routine changed, so nothing about the security did either. This course is about the routine. Where a check runs. What it is allowed to stop. Who reads it, and when. {{routine}} You will work on one small service, called linkbox. It turns a long address into a short one. You inherit it, with four security defects in it. {{linkbox}} Each lesson adds a check to its pipeline. The check finds a defect, and you fix it with a test that proves the fix. {{pipeline}} Today you build the lab all of that runs on. Docker, the project, and a CI server of your own, small enough to read in full. {{lab}} By the end of the lesson, a push on your own machine runs the tests, builds an image, and tells you about every step it took. {{push}}
